headline: Sensex slips over 600 points, Nifty tests 22,600 amid high crude oil prices and sector sell-offs

marketStatus.message: Market is open for trading today.

why: Crude oil prices topping $110 per barrel put heavy pressure on Indian equity markets.
RBI minutes signaled potential further interest rate hikes, keeping bond yields steady and equities cautious.
Declines in power, metal, and FMCG sectors dragged key benchmark indices lower.
Traders trimmed positions ahead of the US Federal Reserve meeting next week.
whatHappening: Sensex dropped over 600 points to fall below 22,600 while Nifty hovered near 22,600-22,700 levels.
Jio Platforms' IPO retail segment got fully subscribed, bringing total overall subscription to 3.71 times.
Gold prices fell by Rs 2,000 per 10 grams and silver plunged Rs 6,000 per kg.
IGI shares locked in a 10% upper circuit after reporting a 43% YoY jump in Q2 profit.
summary: Indian benchmark indices experienced a sharp sell-off today, with the Sensex tumbling over 600 points below 22,600. Soaring crude oil prices above $110 and hawkish RBI minutes created headwinds across sectors like FMCG, power, and metals. On stock-specific actions, IGI surged 10% on strong Q2 profit growth, while Maruti Suzuki and Tata Steel dragged markets lower.
